however, note that a looser sleeve style allows for more flexibility in design changes. - Pay attention to the foot of the sleeve, ensuring it is not sharp. ### Overall Shape Assessment - Evaluate the sleeve length and consider adding a rectangular sleeve plate for symmetry. - Use Ctrl + D to duplicate the sleeve plate symmetrically and arrange it using Shift + F. ## Troubleshooting Sleeve Issues ### Addressing Inconsistent Curves - Smooth out any inconsistent curves on the sleeve to maintain a cohesive design. - If a section of the curve appears abrupt, adjust the sleeve points to create a smoother transition. ## Modifying the Jacket Design ### Collar Adjustments - Begin by cutting back the collar and transforming it into a straight line. - Gradually shape the collar into a refined design to fit the overall garment aesthetic. ### Adding Details - Utilize the editing panel tool to refine the collar's position, ensuring it aligns with the intended neckline. - Create a rectangular plate for the collar and sew it onto the jacket, using the correct sewing machine settings. ## Finalizing Design Elements ### Panel Merging and Layering - Merge the lines effectively to create a seamless look. - Ensure that all layers are properly aligned and that excess curves are removed for a clean finish. ### Simulation and Review - After making the necessary adjustments, simulate the garment to observe how the changes affect the overall design. - Adjust the bending strength and elasticity settings to achieve the desired visual effects. ## Conclusion The trench coat production involves meticulous attention to detail, from adjusting sleeve lengths to refining collar shapes. By managing simulations effectively and making iterative adjustments, we can achieve a polished final product.
